_comment: The authored world: what can be observed, and the thoughts that come of it. Empty on purpose -- the shore is being authored from scratch. `config/psyche.placeholder.json` holds the old test content and is a reference for the authoring format (encounter shape, tiers, deeds, unlock_when clauses); it is NOT loaded. An encounter must author both halves -- something to observe AND something to do -- or it is dropped at load with a warning. Any text field may carry {player} -- it binds to the pilgrim's chosen name at world-enter. Tunable -- edit + relaunch (dev reads assets from source).

roll._comment: Tuning for the thought roll + reward scaling. Coefficients only; the math lives in C++ (see include/Psyche.h RollConfig). THE DENSITY RULE: a reading pays nothing of itself -- exp_discovery is paid ONCE for finding a spot at all, exp_per_value scales a THOUGHT (the largest reward -- understanding is the subject), and a flag pays by what it opened: exp_flag_read when something gates on it, exp_flag_goal when it closes an authored thread, nothing when it is incidental.

_interact_reach_comment: World px from an encounter's box edge: get within this WHILE FACING IT and it lights and can be observed. A world tile is 32px, so 72 is a bit over two tiles -- you notice a thing from across a small room, not only nose-to-nose. Facing is what keeps the wider reach unambiguous. One knob for the whole game.
_notebook_comment: A THOUGHT IS THE NOTEBOOK -- it is where he articulates what he never says aloud, so without one nothing finishes becoming a thought: it stays unfired (and lands the moment he is carrying one) while `want_text` surfaces instead, once per stretch of not having it. A delay, never a loss. Remarks are exempt: speech needs no page. `item` empty turns the rule off.

notebook.want_text: Something worth keeping -- and nothing to keep it in.

encounters._comment: the wake-up moment, fired by the wake scene (never placed). No speaker: the tier is HIS half-asleep read of the room, and the menu is the game's first decision -- a must_choose menu, so it repeats until a deed CONSUMES it. The turn-offs are the room's chores (each one_shot, each raising the flag its sound dies on); doing BOTH unlocks get_up. Hiding is always available -- and if he hides, Mom silences the room herself (mom_enters). This beat is the first stroke of who this Will is.

tiers.text: The alarm again. The TV downstairs, or maybe in the room. Morning has opinions.

add.label: Turn off the TV.
add.result_text: A reach, a button. The murmur stops mid-sentence.

add.label: Pull the covers over your head.
add.result_text: Warm. Dark. For a little while, no such thing as today.
add._minutes_comment: 'for a little while' is the joke and the cost: the morning gets away from him again.

encounters._comment: the alarm clock. Its loop rings until this deed sets alarm_off (leaving it on is a choice). Needs an Encounter placement on the clock in PlayerRoom.

tiers.text: The clock, mid-argument with the morning. It has been winning for a while.

encounters._comment: the TV. Its murmur runs until turn_off sets tv_off (the shutdown clunk fires on the same flag). Needs an Encounter placement on the TV in PlayerRoom.

tiers.text: Static, mostly. It kept somebody company all night.

add.label: Turn it off.
add.result_text: The picture folds into a point and is gone.

encounters._comment: the covers branch's exchange at the bedside, fired by the mom_enters scene AFTER her call through the door (the first_morning_call remark). trigger Enter + speaker = her voice, unprompted. The tier carries the beat's one job: the promise to Mr. Richards (the trail). Deeds are the player's replies; result lines are hers -- and either reply sets mom_mentioned_trail, because however he answers, he has now been told, and the errand is on his agenda.
encounters.speaker: mom

tiers.text: You promised Mr. Richards you'd clear the trail in his backyard today. Up.

add.label: I'm up. I'm up.
add.result_text: Mm. The kettle's on. He's expecting you before it gets hot out.

add.label: Five more minutes.
add.result_text: You said that yesterday, and the day still came. Boots by the door.

encounters._comment: the slipped-out branch: her voice from downstairs when your door goes. Enter + speaker = spoken. Her line carries the SAME errand mom_enters delivers at the bedside, so its reply sets mom_mentioned_trail too -- whichever way the morning went, he has been told, and the trail is on his agenda. The deed also satisfies the both-halves rule; it is unreachable outside the scene (no placement).
encounters.speaker: mom

tiers.text: {player}…? That you? -- Don't forget Mr. Richards. The trail. You promised.

add.label: Yeah -- I'm up.
add.result_text: Breakfast's out. Don't let it sit.

encounters._comment: shape is final, words are a first draft to rewrite. One encounter = the whole person; tiers are what HE notices (his voice), deeds are his moves, result_text is HER voice (speaker). The chain demonstrated: observe her -> a thought lands -> the thought's id unlocks a deed -> her reply sets a flag -> a second thought builds on both.
encounters.speaker: mom

tiers.text: She is at the counter, already dressed. The kettle has been on a while.
She moves like the kitchen is a place she is holding still. Everything wiped twice.

add.label: Say good morning
add.result_text: Morning. There's toast, if you'll actually eat this time.

add._comment: Unlocked by NOTICING, not by menu-grinding: the thought below must land first.
add.label: Ask if she slept
add.result_text: I sleep fine. You're the one leaving with half a plan -- sit, eat something.

encounters._comment: the errand made physical, at the mouth of the trail. Observing it is his own read of the storm's leavings. The WORK is not this menu -- it is the four piles themselves (placed takeable things on the map, drawing from the storm_debris yield table): hauling each one off is what opens the path and what puts the first materials in his satchel. This spot is the reading and the standing-back-to-look; richards_debris_cleared is raised by the last pile leaving, not by a deed here.

tiers.text: The storm put half a tree across the path. Branches, mostly -- the kind of mess that looks worse than it is.
Not one fall but two: an old break, grey and dry, under this week's green wood. The path has been closing for longer than a week.

add.label: Size up the work.
add.result_text: Four piles, give or take. An hour of hauling if he doesn't stop to admire it.

encounters._comment: Mr Richards himself. Shape follows mom's: one encounter = the whole person, tiers are what WILL notices (his voice), deeds are Will's moves, result_text is Richards'. The character note that drives everything: he is not a messy man, he is a man whose body stopped letting him do the things he used to. The unfinished jobs around his property ARE that, and noticing it is the tier-2 reading. He asks for the trail AGAIN -- this is routine between them, a favour years old, not a quest he is handing out.
encounters.speaker: mr_richards

tiers.text: Mr. Richards is out front, in the chair he keeps by the door. He lifts a hand before you are close enough to hear him.

The rake has been against the fence long enough to mark it. A tin of nails on the step, opened, not used. Nothing here is untidy -- everything is simply where it was set down and never picked back up.

add.label: Say hello.
add.result_text: Oh -- hello, Will. Thank you for coming out. That storm made a mess of my trail again, and my old bones could never clear it the way you do.

add._comment: Unlocked by NOTICING, not by menu-grinding -- the tier-2 reading of his property is what makes the question askable. He answers plainly; there is no self-pity in him.
add.label: Ask if there is anything else.
add.say: Is there anything else that wants doing?
add.result_text: Ha. There is always something else. Get the trail open and we will call it square -- I have been looking at that rake for a fortnight and it has not moved yet.

thoughts._comment: Perception: noticing her, from observing her. Its id becomes a memory that unlocks the ask.
thoughts.text: She was up before the kettle. The tired sits on her like it lives here.
thoughts.miss_text: Something about the way she stands. It slips away.

thoughts._comment: Reason: fusing the noticing with her deflection. emotional_weight carries it -- it opens nothing, it just matters.
thoughts.text: She answers questions about herself by feeding people. That is the whole answer.
thoughts.miss_text: Her answer wasn't an answer, but you can't say what it was instead.

thoughts._comment: what the work leaves him with -- reachable only after the clearing, so it is the errand's echo rather than a thing he could think about it beforehand.
thoughts.text: Nobody watched him do it. The path is open anyway.

thoughts._comment: What the second look at his property adds up to. Not pity -- a recognition, and the thing that turns an errand into a kindness. Reachable only from the deeper reading, so it belongs to the player who looked twice.
thoughts.text: He did not stop caring about the place. His body stopped agreeing to it.

remarks._comment: her call through the bedroom door, played by the mom_enters scene BEFORE she enters -- reading it is what brings her in. No unlock_when: scene-only (nothing triggers it ambiently).
the game's first words, said into the pillow. Faculty-less so it always lands; remarks never reach the notebook.

the cost of sleeping on it. Not a fail state -- the errand is still there to discharge -- just the house noticing. Reachable only from day 2 with the work still undone (`without` the goal flag), so doing it on day 1 means these words never exist.
remarks.text: Mr. Richards asked after you. I told him you'd been very busy.

remarks._comment: his half of the same joke, in his own register: drier, and he does not pretend it was busyness.
remarks.text: Path's still there. Storm hasn't moved it for me yet.
